mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (HOUST) above 1.3 million units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives corporate revenue expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1300.0, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 103.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity and economic contraction, which triggers risk-off sentiment and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 103.0, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL above 3.5% and FEDFUNDS above 4.3% signals persistent inflation and a restrictive monetary policy regime, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and FEDFUNDS > 4.3, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS above 160,000 and a decline in UNRATE below 4.1% signals a strong labor market with rising employment and tightening conditions, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with wage pressure
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 160000 and UNRATE < 4.1, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) above 725,000 million dollars, combined with rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1.3 million units, signals strong aggregate demand and consumer confidence, which drives corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 725000 and HOUST > 1300.0, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.5% annualized growth, observed over the prior four quarters, signals strong underlying economic momentum that supports corporate profitability and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
